title: Recall first, then refine: how the real top-3 emerges from a top-10

events.label: Ask the question
events.detail: "Who pays return shipping for cross-city returns?" — the answer hides in one section of the store, and its wording barely overlaps the query.

events.label: Vector search (top-10)
events.detail: bi-encoder architecture: query and document are embedded independently, then compared — fast enough to fish candidates from a hundred thousand chunks in milliseconds; but the two texts never 'meet', so precision is limited.

events.label: top-10 goes to the reranker
events.detail: The wide-net 10 candidates go to precision ranking — this step can afford to be slow, because the set is small.

events.label: Score each candidate jointly
events.detail: cross-encoder: the query and each document are concatenated and passed through the model together, so word-level interactions are fully visible — accurate but slow, worthy only of small sets.

events.label: Scores rearranged
events.detail: The original 7th is rescored at 0.96 and rises to 1st — it matches 'cross-city' with 'different-region', little lexical overlap that the two-tower model cannot see; the cross-encoder catches it at a glance.

events.label: The final top-3 decided
events.detail: Post-rerank top-3 = former 7th, 1st, and 4th. Recall guarantees 'not missing', reranking guarantees 'not messy' — each stage its own job.

events.label: Position bias
events.detail: Chunks ranked higher are more readily trusted by the LLM — reranking not only picks the right chunks but puts the right ones first.

events.label: top-3 enters the prompt
events.detail: Three chunks go to the model with the query — the prompt fits only these, so 'the top 3 decide the answer quality'.

events.label: Answer generated
events.detail: "For cross-city returns, shipping is paid by the buyer unless agreed otherwise." — cited from the post-rerank 1st chunk (formerly 7th).

events.label: Delivered
events.detail: The answer carries provenance (section path). The whole chain: recall 10 → rerank 3 → generate 1 answer.

events.label: The price of skipping the reranker
events.detail: Skip reranking and the target chunk stays 7th; if the prompt fits only the top-3, the answer chunk never reaches the model — reranking is the quality gate that presses 50 down to 3.
